ai.prompt: Ipaliwanag nang simple ang Section 6.3 ng CAO 01-2025 tungkol sa mga obligasyon ng accredited e-Commerce stakeholders sa ilalim ng Internet Transactions Act of 2023. Magbigay ng practical example, banggitin ang related provisions, at linawin ang common misconceptions.

paragraphs.text: Identification of the person or persons on whose behalf the e-Commerce transaction is made;

ai.title: Identification ng Pinagsasagawaan ng Transaksyon
ai.content:
📖 Kahulugan: Dapat matukoy kung sino ang tao o mga taong pinagsasagawaan ng e-Commerce transaction.

💡 Simpleng Paliwanag: Dapat malinaw kung para kanino ang bilihan, hindi lang ang username o account.

⚠️ Dapat Tandaan: Isa ito sa obligasyon ng accredited stakeholders. Kaugnay nito ang buyer at seller data sa e-CIFCM (Sec. 7.2).
ai.prompt: Ipaliwanag nang simple ang Section 6.3.1 ng CAO 01-2025 tungkol sa identification ng taong pinagsasagawaan ng e-Commerce transaction. Magbigay ng practical example, ipaliwanag kung bakit ito mahalaga, at linawin ang common misconceptions.

paragraphs.text: Prohibition of the sale of regulated goods unless the necessary permits and license information are submitted, including the import commodity clearance mark, if applicable, and contractual obligations on the compliance with sale procedures and limitations, and other relevant conditions for the sale as may be imposed by any law or local government regulation; and

ai.title: Regulated Goods at Permits
ai.content:
📖 Kahulugan: Bawal ibenta ang regulated goods maliban kung naisumite ang kinakailangang permits at license information, kasama ang import commodity clearance mark kung applicable, at ang contractual obligations sa pagsunod sa sale procedures at limitations, at iba pang kondisyon na itinakda ng batas o local government regulation.

💡 Simpleng Paliwanag: Para sa regulated goods, kailangang may permit at lisensya bago mailagay sa bentahan.

📦 Halimbawa: Kung ang item ay nangangailangan ng permit mula sa regulatory agency, kailangang naisumite ang permit info bago ito maibenta sa platform.

⚠️ Dapat Tandaan: Kasama ang import commodity clearance mark kung applicable. Tingnan din ang Sec. 10.4 at Sec. 11.
ai.prompt: Ipaliwanag nang simple ang Section 6.3.2 ng CAO 01-2025 tungkol sa pagbabawal sa pagbebenta ng regulated goods nang walang permits. Magbigay ng practical customs example, ipaliwanag ang import commodity clearance mark, banggitin ang Sec. 11, at linawin ang common misconceptions.

paragraphs.text: Protection of Data Privacy Rights of Consumers shall be strictly observed, in accordance with Republic Act No. 10173 or the “Data Privacy Act of 2012”.

ai.title: Data Privacy ng Consumers
ai.content:
📖 Kahulugan: Mahigpit na susundin ang proteksyon ng data privacy rights ng consumers ayon sa RA 10173 (Data Privacy Act of 2012).

💡 Simpleng Paliwanag: Hindi basta-basta puwedeng gamitin o ilabas ang personal data ng buyers. Mahalaga ito dahil ang e-CIFCM ay may pangalan, phone number, email, at address ng buyer.

⚠️ Dapat Tandaan: RA 10173 ang batas. Ang BOC mismo ay may confidentiality obligation sa Sec. 13.
ai.prompt: Ipaliwanag nang simple ang Section 6.3.3 ng CAO 01-2025 tungkol sa Data Privacy Rights ng consumers. Magbigay ng practical example gamit ang buyer data sa e-CIFCM, banggitin ang RA 10173 at Sec. 13, at linawin ang common misconceptions.

paragraphs.text: The digital platform providers and e-retailers shall generate the data required by BOC from their respective platform systems and shall be made available to the clearance agents for compliance with the submission of the e-Manifest as required in the CAO.

ai.title: Data Mula sa Platforms
ai.content:
📖 Kahulugan: Ang digital platform providers at e-retailers ang gagawa ng data na kailangan ng BOC mula sa kanilang platform systems at ibibigay ito sa clearance agents para masunod ang pagsusumite ng e-Manifest na hinihingi ng CAO.

💡 Simpleng Paliwanag: Platform ang pinagmumulan ng data, at ang clearance agent ang magsusumite nito sa BOC.

⚠️ Dapat Tandaan: Hatian ng responsibilidad: DPP at e-retailer ang nag-generate ng data, clearance agent ang nagsusumite. Ang laman ng kailangang data ay nasa Sec. 7.2.
ai.prompt: Ipaliwanag nang simple ang Section 6.4 ng CAO 01-2025 tungkol sa pagbibigay ng platforms ng data sa clearance agents. Magbigay ng practical customs example, ipaliwanag ang hatian ng responsibilidad, banggitin ang Sec. 7, at linawin ang common misconceptions.

paragraphs.text: The Bureau shall issue the necessary guidelines and procedures and the conditions for the accreditation of the various e-Commerce stakeholders.

ai.title: Guidelines para sa Accreditation
ai.content:
📖 Kahulugan: Maglalabas ang BOC ng guidelines, procedures, at conditions para sa accreditation ng iba't ibang e-Commerce stakeholders.

💡 Simpleng Paliwanag: Hindi nakalagay sa CAO ang buong proseso ng accreditation. Hiwalay na issuance ang magdedetalye nito.

⚠️ Dapat Tandaan: Hindi kumpleto ang CAO pagdating sa accreditation details. Kailangan mo ring hanapin ang guidelines na ilalabas ng BOC.
ai.prompt: Ipaliwanag nang simple ang Section 6.5 ng CAO 01-2025 tungkol sa guidelines at conditions ng accreditation. Magbigay ng practical example, ipaliwanag kung bakit hiwalay ang guidelines, at linawin ang common misconceptions.

paragraphs.text: Prior to the arrival of the shipments and to enable the processing of e-Commerce goods, the appointed freight forwarder, NVOCC, consolidator or Clearance Agent shall submit to the Bureau a true, complete and detailed e-CIFCM, within the mandated cut-off period under existing laws, rules, and regulations. Subject to the application of risk-based management techniques, the Bureau may allow the advanced processing of e-Commerce goods, as may be warranted.

ai.title: Pagsusumite ng e-CIFCM
ai.content:
📖 Kahulugan: Bago dumating ang shipments, ang appointed freight forwarder, NVOCC, consolidator, o Clearance Agent ay dapat magsumite sa BOC ng true, complete, at detailed e-CIFCM sa loob ng mandated cut-off period. Depende sa risk-based management techniques, puwedeng payagan ng BOC ang advanced processing ng e-Commerce goods.

💡 Simpleng Paliwanag: Maagang manifest ang susi para mapabilis ang processing. Kapag mababa ang risk, puwedeng i-process nang maaga.

📦 Halimbawa: Bago lumapag ang eroplano, naipasa na ng appointed forwarder ang e-CIFCM para sa 500 parcel. Dahil low-risk ang karamihan, puwede na silang ma-process nang maaga.

⚠️ Dapat Tandaan: Apat ang puwedeng magsumite: freight forwarder, NVOCC, consolidator, Clearance Agent. Dapat true, complete, at detailed ang e-CIFCM. Ang cut-off period ay nasa existing rules, hindi tinukoy sa CAO na ito.
ai.prompt: Ipaliwanag nang simple ang Section 7.1 ng CAO 01-2025 tungkol sa pagsusumite ng e-CIFCM bago dumating ang shipments. Magbigay ng practical customs example, ipaliwanag ang advanced processing at risk-based management, at linawin ang common misconceptions.

paragraphs.text:
For purposes of identifying the individual e-Commerce shipments consigned to the ultimate consignees, the e-CIFCM must contain the following information:
DATA ELEMENT | DESCRIPTION
MBL Number | Master Bill of Lading Number
HBL Number | House Bill of Lading Number
Number of Packages | Number of individual item packages in such a way that they cannot be divided without first undoing the packing
Description of Goods | Description of goods per item
Declared Value per Item | FOB/FCA Value per item
Gross Weight | Total weight
Registry Number | Flight Number/Vessel Registry
Date of Arrival | Date on which an aircraft / vessel arrive at its destination port
Marks and Numbers | Per individual cartons, drums, boxes, crates and other forms of protective packaging
Type of Packages | Cartons, boxes, etc.
Country of Origin | Country where goods originated
Seller's Name | Name of a party selling merchandise to a buyer
Seller's Address | Address of a party selling merchandise to a buyer
Seller's Identifier | Tax Identification Number of the party selling merchandise to a buyer, if applicable.
Buyer's Name | Name of the buyer or the ultimate consignee of the e-Commerce merchandise
Buyer's Phone number | Phone number of the buyer
Buyer's Email Address | e-Mail address of the buyer
Buyer's Address | Address of the buyer
Digital Platform Provider / e-marketplace / e-retailer / Website | Name of the trading party in digital platform/marketplace and e-retailer website where the sale is transacted
Digital Platform / e-Marketplace/ e-retailer / Website URL | URL of the digital platform/marketplace and e-retailer website where the sale is transacted
Order Number / Tracking Number | Unique purchase order or tracking number assigned by the digital platform/marketplace and e-retailer website
Intrinsic value | Price in Export Country or Listed Price in digital platform/marketplace and e-retailer website
Port Code | Collection District / Port Code

ai.title: Required Data Elements ng e-CIFCM
ai.content:
📖 Kahulugan: Para matukoy ang bawat individual e-Commerce shipment na naka-consign sa ultimate consignees, may 23 data elements na dapat laman ng e-CIFCM, mula sa MBL Number hanggang Port Code.

💡 Simpleng Paliwanag: Parang checklist ng impormasyong dapat kumpleto: transport document numbers (MBL, HBL), detalye ng goods (packages, description, value, weight, marks, type, country of origin), detalye ng biyahe (registry number, date of arrival, port code), detalye ng seller (name, address, identifier), detalye ng buyer (name, phone, email, address), at detalye ng platform (name, URL, order o tracking number, intrinsic value).

📦 Halimbawa: Parcel na may listed price na P3,000 sa platform. Sa e-CIFCM, ilalagay ang P3,000 bilang intrinsic value at ang FOB/FCA value nito bilang declared value per item, kasama ang buyer details at order number.

⚠️ Dapat Tandaan: Ang Declared Value per Item ay FOB/FCA value. Ang Intrinsic Value ay presyo sa export country o listed price sa platform (Sec. 3.27). Ang Seller's Identifier ay TIN kung applicable. Kasama ang parehong MBL at HBL numbers.
ai.prompt: Ipaliwanag nang simple ang Section 7.2 ng CAO 01-2025 at ang mga data elements na dapat nasa e-CIFCM. Magbigay ng practical customs example ng pagpuno ng e-CIFCM, ipaliwanag ang pagkakaiba ng Declared Value per Item at Intrinsic value, at linawin ang common misconceptions.

paragraphs.text: Cargoes not listed in the e-CICFM shall be duly covered by a supplemental manifest which shall be submitted within six (6) hours upon arrival of the carrying aircraft or vessel.

ai.title: Supplemental Manifest
ai.content:
📖 Kahulugan: Ang cargoes na wala sa e-CIFCM (e-CICFM sa teksto) ay dapat saklawin ng supplemental manifest na isusumite sa loob ng anim (6) na oras pagdating ng sasakyang panghimpapawid o pandagat.

💡 Simpleng Paliwanag: Kung may nakaligtaang kargamento sa manifest, may anim na oras ang forwarder para maghabol pagdating ng carrier.

📦 Halimbawa: Dumating ang eroplano ng 8:00 AM at may 20 parcel na hindi nailista. Dapat maisumite ang supplemental manifest bago mag-2:00 PM.

⚠️ Dapat Tandaan: Six (6) hours mula arrival. Kapag hindi nasunod, posibleng maging unmanifested goods na may fines at penalties (Sec. 7.4).
ai.prompt: Ipaliwanag nang simple ang Section 7.3 ng CAO 01-2025 tungkol sa supplemental manifest na isusumite sa loob ng 6 oras mula arrival. Magbigay ng practical customs example, ipaliwanag kung bakit ito umiiral, ikonekta sa Sec. 7.4, at linawin ang common misconceptions.

paragraphs.text: Unmanifested goods shall be subject to fines and penalties as provided under the CMTA and existing rules and regulations.

ai.title: Unmanifested Goods
ai.content:
📖 Kahulugan: Ang unmanifested goods ay papatawan ng fines at penalties ayon sa CMTA at umiiral na rules at regulations.

💡 Simpleng Paliwanag: Kapag hindi nailista sa manifest at hindi rin nasaklaw ng supplemental manifest, may parusa.

⚠️ Dapat Tandaan: Ang eksaktong fines at penalties ay nasa CMTA at iba pang rules, hindi sa CAO na ito. Kaugnay ng 6-hour rule sa Sec. 7.3.
ai.prompt: Ipaliwanag nang simple ang Section 7.4 ng CAO 01-2025 tungkol sa unmanifested goods. Magbigay ng practical customs example, ikonekta sa Sec. 7.3 at sa CMTA, at linawin ang common misconceptions.

paragraphs.text: The HAWB or HBL of each ultimate consignee must be submitted by the appointed freight forwarder, NVOCC, consolidator or Clearance Agent to the Bureau's automated system in accordance with existing Customs rules and regulations.

ai.title: Pagsusumite ng HAWB o HBL
ai.content:
📖 Kahulugan: Ang HAWB o HBL ng bawat ultimate consignee ay dapat isumite ng appointed freight forwarder, NVOCC, consolidator, o Clearance Agent sa automated system ng BOC, ayon sa umiiral na Customs rules.

💡 Simpleng Paliwanag: Bawat buyer ay may sariling house bill (HAWB para sa air, HBL para sa sea), at lahat ng iyon ay kailangang maisumite sa system.

⚠️ Dapat Tandaan: Per ultimate consignee ang HAWB o HBL, at sa automated system ng BOC isinusumite. Ito ang house-level na dokumento sa ilalim ng master AWB o BL.
ai.prompt: Ipaliwanag nang simple ang Section 7.5 ng CAO 01-2025 tungkol sa pagsusumite ng HAWB o HBL ng bawat ultimate consignee. Magbigay ng practical customs example, ipaliwanag kung bakit ito kailangan, at linawin ang common misconceptions.

paragraphs.text: The Bureau shall issue the relevant Customs Memorandum Order (CMO) providing the procedures for the release of e-Commerce goods.

ai.title: Customs Clearance Formalities
ai.content:
📖 Kahulugan: Maglalabas ang BOC ng relevant Customs Memorandum Order (CMO) na magbibigay ng procedures para sa release ng e-Commerce goods.

💡 Simpleng Paliwanag: Ang CAO ay policy at framework. Ang CMO naman ang karaniwang gamit ng BOC para sa operational procedures. Kaya hindi mo mahahanap sa CAO na ito ang step-by-step na release process.

⚠️ Dapat Tandaan: Dalawang magkaibang issuance: CAO (administrative order, policy) at CMO (memorandum order, operational). Para sa detalye ng release, kailangan mong hanapin ang CMO na ilalabas.
ai.prompt: Ipaliwanag nang simple ang Section 8 (Customs Clearance Formalities) ng CAO 01-2025. Ano ang pagkakaiba ng CAO at CMO? Magbigay ng practical example, banggitin ang related provisions, at linawin ang common misconceptions.

paragraphs.text: The Bureau shall impose import processing charges on e-Commerce goods that fall within the De Minimis threshold as may be provided under existing rules and regulations.

ai.title: Import Processing Charge
ai.content:
📖 Kahulugan: Magpapataw ang BOC ng import processing charges sa e-Commerce goods na pasok sa De Minimis threshold, ayon sa umiiral na rules at regulations.

💡 Simpleng Paliwanag: Kahit walang duty at tax ang goods na pasok sa de minimis, may processing charge pa rin dahil may gastos sa pag-process nito.

📦 Halimbawa: Parcel na FOB value P5,000 (Category 2): walang duty at tax, pero may import processing charge.

⚠️ Dapat Tandaan: Sa goods na pasok sa De Minimis ito ipinapataw. Ang halaga ay ayon sa existing rules, hindi tinukoy sa CAO. Ang EPS fee ay may 10% cap ng Import Processing Fee (Sec. 5.6).
ai.prompt: Ipaliwanag nang simple ang Section 9 (Import Processing Charge) ng CAO 01-2025. Magbigay ng practical example ng Category 2 goods na may processing charge, ikonekta sa De Minimis at Sec. 5.6, at linawin ang common misconceptions.

sections.heading: Section 10. Exclusion from e-Commerce Goods Processing

paragraphs.text: The following importations shall not be processed as e-Commerce goods:

ai.title: Panimula sa Exclusions
ai.content:
📖 Kahulugan: Introduction ito sa mga importations na hindi ipo-process bilang e-Commerce goods. May anim na item, 10.1 hanggang 10.6.

💡 Simpleng Paliwanag: Hindi sila dadaan sa e-Commerce processing lane, pero hindi ibig sabihing bawal silang ipasok. Iba lang ang proseso nila.

⚠️ Dapat Tandaan: Ang 'excluded' ay hindi 'prohibited'. Tandaan kung alin ang may kondisyon (10.2 at 10.4) at alin ang buo (10.3, 10.5).
ai.prompt: Ipaliwanag nang simple ang panimula ng Section 10 ng CAO 01-2025 tungkol sa mga importations na hindi ipo-process bilang e-Commerce goods. Magbigay ng practical example, ipaliwanag kung bakit may exclusions, at linawin ang common misconceptions.

paragraphs.text: Importations declared as “without commercial value”, “of no commercial value” or with specific amount but qualified by the phrase “for customs purposes” or analogous phrases.

ai.title: Exclusion: Without Commercial Value
ai.content:
📖 Kahulugan: Hindi ipo-process bilang e-Commerce goods ang importations na idineklarang 'without commercial value' o 'of no commercial value', o may tiyak na halaga pero may pariralang 'for customs purposes' o katulad nito.

💡 Simpleng Paliwanag: Hindi puwedeng gumamit ng ganitong mga salita para makaiwas sa tamang value declaration.

⚠️ Dapat Tandaan: Kasama ang analogous phrases. Basahin ang karugtong na talata para sa kinakailangang declaration.
ai.prompt: Ipaliwanag nang simple ang Section 10.1 ng CAO 01-2025 tungkol sa importations na idineklarang without commercial value. Magbigay ng practical customs example, ipaliwanag kung bakit ito exclusion, at linawin ang common misconceptions.

paragraphs.text: Hence, the freight forwarder, NVOCC, consolidator or Clearance Agent must declare the specific value of the goods supported by available invoice, receipt, or equivalent document, if any, except for Correspondences and Documents classified under Category 1 of the WCO Guidelines for the Immediate Release of Consignments by Customs;

ai.title: Dapat Ideklara ang Specific Value
ai.content:
📖 Kahulugan: Kailangang ideklara ng freight forwarder, NVOCC, consolidator, o Clearance Agent ang specific value ng goods, suportado ng invoice, resibo, o katumbas na dokumento kung mayroon. May exception ang Correspondence and Documents na Category 1 ng WCO Guidelines for the Immediate Release of Consignments.

💡 Simpleng Paliwanag: Kahit sabihing 'no commercial value', kailangan pa ring may tunay na halagang idedeklara.

⚠️ Dapat Tandaan: Karugtong ito ng Sec. 10.1. Exception: Category 1 lang. Hindi puwedeng gamitin ang 'no commercial value' bilang shortcut.
ai.prompt: Ipaliwanag nang simple ang karugtong ng Section 10.1 ng CAO 01-2025 tungkol sa kailangang declaration ng specific value at sa exception para sa Category 1. Magbigay ng practical example, banggitin ang WCO Guidelines, at linawin ang common misconceptions.

paragraphs.text: Importations classified under Business-to-Business (B2B) transactions as defined under the Internet Transactions Act and which are not purchased through an accredited online platform;

ai.title: Exclusion: B2B na Hindi sa Accredited Platform
ai.content:
📖 Kahulugan: Hindi ipo-process bilang e-Commerce goods ang importations na B2B transactions ayon sa Internet Transactions Act at hindi binili sa accredited online platform.

💡 Simpleng Paliwanag: Dalawang kondisyon ang kailangan: B2B ito AT hindi sa accredited online platform binili.

⚠️ Dapat Tandaan: Hindi lahat ng B2B ang excluded, kundi ang B2B na hindi sa accredited online platform lang.
ai.prompt: Ipaliwanag nang simple ang Section 10.2 ng CAO 01-2025 tungkol sa B2B importations na hindi binili sa accredited online platform. Magbigay ng practical customs example, ipaliwanag ang dalawang kondisyon, at linawin ang common misconceptions.

paragraphs.text: Importations classified under Consumer-to-Consumer (C2C) transactions as defined under the Internet Transactions Act;

ai.title: Exclusion: C2C
ai.content:
📖 Kahulugan: Hindi ipo-process bilang e-Commerce goods ang importations na C2C transactions ayon sa Internet Transactions Act.

💡 Simpleng Paliwanag: Kapag consumer-to-consumer ang bilihan, hindi ito sakop ng e-Commerce processing.

⚠️ Dapat Tandaan: Lahat ng C2C ay excluded, walang dagdag na kondisyon. Magkaiba ito sa B2B na may kondisyon (Sec. 10.2).
ai.prompt: Ipaliwanag nang simple ang Section 10.3 ng CAO 01-2025 tungkol sa C2C importations bilang exclusion. Magbigay ng practical customs example, ihambing sa 10.2, at linawin ang common misconceptions.

paragraphs.text: Goods including those with De Minimis Value subject to the requirements or conditions imposed by the concerned regulatory agency unless for personal use and within the limits allowed by regulation;

ai.title: Exclusion: Goods na May Regulatory Requirements
ai.content:
📖 Kahulugan: Hindi ipo-process bilang e-Commerce goods ang goods, kasama ang may De Minimis Value, na may requirements o conditions mula sa concerned regulatory agency, maliban kung para sa personal use at nasa loob ng limits na pinapayagan ng regulasyon.

💡 Simpleng Paliwanag: Kahit mura at pasok sa de minimis, kung may permit o requirement mula sa ahensya, hindi ito sa e-Commerce lane dadaan, maliban kung personal use at nasa allowed limits.

📦 Halimbawa: Item na FOB value P2,000 pero nangangailangan ng permit ng regulatory agency. Hindi ito automatic na e-Commerce lane dahil lang mura.

⚠️ Dapat Tandaan: Exception: personal use AT nasa allowed limits. Dalawang kondisyon ito. Kaugnay ng Sec. 6.3.2 at Sec. 11.
ai.prompt: Ipaliwanag nang simple ang Section 10.4 ng CAO 01-2025 tungkol sa goods na may regulatory requirements kahit may de minimis value. Magbigay ng practical customs example, ipaliwanag ang exception para sa personal use, at linawin ang common misconceptions.

paragraphs.text: Importations to be entered conditionally free, for warehousing, for transit and/or admission to free zone; and

ai.title: Exclusion: Conditionally Free, Warehousing, Transit, Free Zone
ai.content:
📖 Kahulugan: Hindi ipo-process bilang e-Commerce goods ang importations na ipapasok nang conditionally free, para sa warehousing, para sa transit, at/o admission sa free zone.

💡 Simpleng Paliwanag: Ibang customs regime ang mga ito, kaya hindi bagay sa simplified e-Commerce process na para sa goods na papasok para sa consumption.

⚠️ Dapat Tandaan: Apat na regime ang nakalista: conditionally free, warehousing, transit, at admission sa free zone. 'And/or' ang wording kaya puwedeng isa o higit pa.
ai.prompt: Ipaliwanag nang simple ang Section 10.5 ng CAO 01-2025 tungkol sa importations na conditionally free, warehousing, transit, at free zone. Magbigay ng practical customs example, ipaliwanag kung bakit excluded, at linawin ang common misconceptions.

paragraphs.text: Other goods as may be recommended and determined by the Commissioner of Customs and approved by the Secretary of Finance.

ai.title: Exclusion: Iba Pang Goods
ai.content:
📖 Kahulugan: Puwedeng magdagdag ng exclusions: iba pang goods na irerekomenda at idedetermina ng Commissioner of Customs at aaprubahan ng Secretary of Finance.

💡 Simpleng Paliwanag: Catch-all ito para flexible ang CAO kung may kategorya ng goods na hindi bagay sa e-Commerce lane.

⚠️ Dapat Tandaan: Dalawang opisyal ang kasali: Commissioner ang nagrerekomenda at nagdedetermina, Secretary of Finance ang nag-aapruba. Hindi sapat ang Commissioner lang.
ai.prompt: Ipaliwanag nang simple ang Section 10.6 ng CAO 01-2025 tungkol sa dagdag na exclusions na idedetermina ng Commissioner at aaprubahan ng Secretary of Finance. Magbigay ng practical example, ipaliwanag ang hatian ng kapangyarihan, at linawin ang common misconceptions.

sections.heading: Section 11. Restrictions on the Importation of Cross-Border e-Commerce Goods

paragraphs.text: Importations of goods classified as prohibited under the CMTA and other laws and regulations shall not be allowed even for e-Commerce purposes. Importations of regulated and restricted goods shall be subject to existing laws and regulations of concerned regulatory agencies.

ai.title: Restrictions sa Importation
ai.content:
📖 Kahulugan: Ang prohibited goods ayon sa CMTA at iba pang batas ay hindi papayagan kahit para sa e-Commerce. Ang regulated at restricted goods ay susunod sa umiiral na batas at regulasyon ng kinauukulang regulatory agencies.

💡 Simpleng Paliwanag: Hindi nagiging legal ang bawal na produkto dahil lang online binili. Ang regulated at restricted ay kailangan pa ring dumaan sa tamang permit o proseso ng ahensya.

📦 Halimbawa: Kahit gaano kababa ang halaga at kahit sa accredited platform binili, kung prohibited ang item, hindi ito papayagang pumasok.

⚠️ Dapat Tandaan: Prohibited: hindi papayagan. Regulated at restricted: susunod sa batas ng ahensya. Tingnan din ang Sec. 6.3.2 at Sec. 10.4.
ai.prompt: Ipaliwanag nang simple ang Section 11 ng CAO 01-2025 tungkol sa prohibited, regulated, at restricted goods sa e-Commerce. Magbigay ng practical customs example, ipaliwanag ang pagkakaiba ng tatlo, ikonekta sa Sec. 6.3.2 at 10.4, at linawin ang common misconceptions.

paragraphs.text: Freight Forwarders accredited by the Bureau to process and release e-Commerce Goods shall open and maintain Prepayment Accounts with the Bureau's in-house bank/Cashier to guarantee the immediate payment of the required duties, taxes, and other charges imposable on the e-Commerce Goods.

ai.title: Prepayment Account
ai.content:
📖 Kahulugan: Ang Freight Forwarders na accredited ng BOC para mag-process at mag-release ng e-Commerce Goods ay dapat magbukas at magpanatili ng Prepayment Accounts sa in-house bank/Cashier ng BOC para masiguro ang agarang bayad ng duties, taxes, at iba pang charges.

💡 Simpleng Paliwanag: May paunang deposito ang forwarder sa BOC para agad mabayaran ang kinakailangang bayarin at mabilis ang release.

📦 Halimbawa: Nag-deposit ang forwarder sa Prepayment Account. Pagka-assess ng duties sa isang Category 3 parcel, sa account na kinukuha ang bayad kaya hindi na kailangang maghintay ng hiwalay na bayaran bago ang release.

⚠️ Dapat Tandaan: Freight Forwarders ang obligado, sa in-house bank/Cashier ng BOC ang account, at ang layunin ay guarantee ng immediate payment. Ito ang praktikal na gamit ng 'account-based system' sa Sec. 4.4.
ai.prompt: Ipaliwanag nang simple ang Section 12 (Prepayment Account) ng CAO 01-2025. Magbigay ng practical customs example kung paano gumagana ang prepayment account, ikonekta sa account-based system sa Sec. 4.4, at linawin ang common misconceptions.

paragraphs.text: The Prepayment Account shall also answer for the amount of duties, taxes, and other charges which should have been collected in cases where mis-sorted or misrouted shipments were not re-exported within twenty-four (24) hours from arrival or, having been exported no proof of landing has been presented.

ai.title: Prepayment Account at Missorted Shipments
ai.content:
📖 Kahulugan: Sasagutin din ng Prepayment Account ang halaga ng duties, taxes, at charges na dapat nakolekta kapag ang mis-sorted o misrouted shipments ay hindi na-re-export sa loob ng 24 oras mula arrival, o na-export pero walang naipakitang proof of landing.

💡 Simpleng Paliwanag: Kung napunta sa maling lugar ang kargamento at hindi naibalik sa loob ng 24 oras, o walang patunay na dumating ito sa pinuntahan, ang prepayment account ang hahabol sa bayarin.

📦 Halimbawa: Misrouted ang parcel at dumating sa Maynila. Hindi ito naibalik sa loob ng 24 oras. Ang halaga ng duties at taxes na dapat nakolekta ay sasagutin ng Prepayment Account ng forwarder.

⚠️ Dapat Tandaan: Dalawang sitwasyon: (1) hindi na-re-export sa loob ng 24 oras mula arrival, o (2) na-export pero walang proof of landing. Kaugnay ng Sec. 4.5.
ai.prompt: Ipaliwanag nang simple ang ikalawang talata ng Section 12 ng CAO 01-2025 tungkol sa prepayment account at mis-sorted o misrouted shipments. Magbigay ng practical customs example ng 24-hour re-export at proof of landing, ikonekta sa Sec. 4.5, at linawin ang common misconceptions.

paragraphs.text: The Bureau shall treat any information or data provided by digital platform providers and e-retailers with utmost confidentiality and for official purposes only pursuant to the Republic Act No. 10173 or the Data Privacy Act of 2012. Any Bureau personnel who utilize said confidential information or use the same other than for official or legal purposes shall be proceeded against under Section 15 of this CAO.

ai.title: Confidentiality of Information
ai.content:

ai.content:

paragraphs.text: This CAO shall take effect thirty (30) days after its complete publication at the Official Gazette or a newspaper of national circulation.

ai.content:

💡 Simpleng Paliwanag: Hindi agad-agad nagiging epektibo ang CAO pagkapirma. Kailangan munang mailathala nang buo, at doon magsisimula ang 30 araw.

📦 Halimbawa: Kung kumpleto ang publication sa ika-1 ng buwan, ang effectivity ay 30 araw pagkatapos ng petsang iyon.

⚠️ Dapat Tandaan: Ang bilang ng 30 days ay mula sa kumpletong publication, hindi mula sa petsa ng pirma ng Commissioner o ng approval ng Secretary of Finance. Mahalaga ang publication para malaman ng publiko ang bagong patakaran.

ai.title: CAO 02-2025: Amendments sa Customs Dues, Fees, and Charges
ai.content:
📖 Kahulugan: Ang CAO 02-2025 ay pag-amyenda at paglilinaw sa CAO 02-2024, ang pangunahing listahan ng customs dues, fees, at charges. Hindi ito bagong buong sistema — ginagawang mas malinaw ang ilang probisyon, nagdaragdag ng bagong Section tungkol sa reimbursement ng travel expenses ng Customs officers, at nagde-defer o nagsu-suspend ng ilang fees.

🔍 Breakdown: Sections 1-7 ay amendments sa specific fees (Vessel Supervision Fee, Underguarding Fee for Transfers, Import Processing Charge, AEO Application Charge, cancellation/modification charges, CDS/DST/LRF). Section 8 ay bagong buong Section tungkol sa Daily Travel Expenses (DTE) at Transportation Expenses. Sections 9-11 ay deferment/suspension ng ilang fees at exemption ng AECOs. Sections 12-14 ay ang Repealing, Separability, at Effectivity Clauses.

💡 Simpleng Paliwanag: Parang updated na 'price list' at 'reimbursement guide' ng Bureau of Customs ito. May bagong rates, may na-clarify na computation (lalo na sa Import Processing Charge ng de minimis goods), at bagong patakaran sa pagbabayad sa mga Customs officer na naka-field duty.

📦 Halimbawa: Isang shipping line ay magbabayad ng Vessel Supervision Fee tuwing dadaong ang barko nila — halimbawa Php 2,250 para sa Boarding Formalities. Samantala, kung may Customs officer na ipinadala sa Cebu para mag-supervise ng isang shipment, puwede na siyang mag-claim ng DTE at Transportation Expenses base sa bagong Section 8.

⭐ Bakit Mahalaga Ito? Direktang nakaka-apekto ito sa babayaran (o mare-reimburse) ng mga customs broker, importer, shipping lines, at Customs personnel sa bawat transaction o paglalakbay.

⚠️ Dapat Tandaan: May mga fees na HINDI pa active — ang Aircraft Supervision Fee ay deferred hanggang May 1, 2025, at ang Certificate of Origin Processing Charge ay temporarily suspended. Huwag ipagpalagay na automatic active lahat ng laman ng CAO 02-2024 dahil may amendments na dito.

🎯 Board Exam Tip: Alamin ang pagkakaiba ng 'deferred' (may tiyak na commencement date — May 1, 2025) laban sa 'suspended' (walang tiyak na petsa, hanggang lifted ng Commissioner with DOF approval).

❓ Madalas Malito ang Students: Tanong — 'Kailan magsisimula ang Aircraft Supervision Fee?' Sagot — Hindi kaagad pagka-effective ng buong CAO; partikular na May 1, 2025 ang commencement nito base sa Section 9.

🔗 Related Topics: CAO No. 02-2024, CAO No. 12-2019 (Transshipment), CAO No. 5-2020 at CMO No. 9-2021 (Express Shipments), Sections 1211, 1508 at 439 ng CMTA, Executive Order No. 77, s. 2019.

Customs Officers rendering services outside of their permanent official stations shall be entitled to payment by the Bureau of Daily Travel Expenses (DTE) and Transportation Expenses, pursuant to Sections 1211 and 1508 of the CMTA, and Executive Order No. 77, s. 2019.

The DTE are amounts authorized to cover expenses for local travel, which consist of (i) costs for hotel accommodation or lodging, including the prescribed taxes and service charges, (ii) meals, and (iii) incidental expenses, including cost for local or inland transportation and reasonable miscellaneous expenses at the place of assignment.

Transportation Expenses are the actual fares of the authorized modes of transportation (e.g., land, sea and air) for local travels from the permanent official station to the destination or place of assignment and back.

💡 Simpleng Paliwanag: Ang DTE ay para sa 'pamumuhay' habang nasa field (tulog, kain, extra gastos); ang Transportation Expenses ay para sa 'biyahe' papunta at pabalik.

ai.title: CAO 02-2024: Customs Dues, Fees, and Charges
ai.content:
📖 Kahulugan: Ang CAO 02-2024 ang nagtatakda ng lahat ng Service Fees, Dues, at Charges na kinokolekta ng Bureau of Customs mula sa mga stakeholders: shipping lines, airlines, air express operators, importers, exporters, customs brokers, freight forwarders, warehouse operators, free zone locators, third party solutions providers, at iba pa. Ipinapatupad nito ang Sec. 204, 1211, 1300, 1301, at 1508 ng CMTA (RA No. 10863).

🔍 Breakdown: Introduction. Sec. 1 Scope. Sec. 2 Objectives (2.1 hanggang 2.3). Sec. 3 Definition of Terms (3.1 hanggang 3.24). Sec. 4 Customs Service Fee (4.1 hanggang 4.12), na napupunta sa Trust Fund. Sec. 5 Customs Dues and Charges (5.1 hanggang 5.34), na napupunta sa General Fund. Sec. 6 CDS, DST, at LRF kada dokumento. Sec. 7 Utilization of Service Fee. Sec. 8 Repealing Clause. Sec. 9 Separability Clause. Sec. 10 Effectivity.

💡 Simpleng Paliwanag: Ito ang 'price list' ng BOC. Dalawa ang pangunahing grupo ng bayarin. Ang Service Fees (Sec. 4) ay bayad sa serbisyo ng Customs personnel, lalo na kapag labas ng Official Work Station o overtime. Ito ay napupunta sa Trust Fund na puwedeng gamitin para sa allowances at overtime ng personnel. Ang Dues and Charges (Sec. 5) ay bayad sa processing, accreditation, certifications, appeals, at iba pa, at napupunta sa General Fund.

📦 Halimbawa: Nag-file ang isang importer ng goods declaration sa Consumption clearance procedure na nasa bracket na above Php 250,000.00 hanggang Php 500,000.00 sa Sec. 5.5.a. Php 1,000.00 ang Import Processing Charge, at hiwalay na idinadagdag ang CDS na Php 100.00 at BIR DST na Php 30.00, kaya Php 1,130.00 ang kabuuan ng tatlo. Kung ipapa-cancel o ipapabago niya ito (hindi dahil sa system error), may hiwalay na singil sa Sec. 5.14: Php 1,000.00 sa first offense, Php 3,000.00 sa second, at Php 5,000.00 sa third o higit pa.

⭐ Bakit Mahalaga Ito? Uniform ang rates, malinaw kung para saan ang bawat bayarin at kung sino ang magbabayad, malinaw kung saan napupunta ang pera (Trust Fund o General Fund), at may mekanismo para mabayaran ang overtime ng Customs personnel.

⚠️ Dapat Tandaan: Sec. 4 = Trust Fund. Sec. 5 = General Fund. Sec. 6: CDS Php 100.00, DST Php 30.00, LRF Php 10.00 kada dokumentong inisyu ng Bureau. Container Security Charge: USD 5 kada TEU (5.34, EO No. 635, s. 2007). Monitoring and Supervision Fee sa third party Service Providers: 10% ng fees collected maliban kung iba ang TOR (4.12). Underguarding fee ay hindi sisingilin kung may E-TRACC, GTSB, o katulad na security measure (4.3 at 4.5). Magiging epektibo ang CAO 30 days after complete publication (Sec. 10).

🎯 Board Exam Tip: Madalas itanong ang pagkakaiba ng Trust Fund at General Fund, ang rates ng Import Processing Charge (5.5.a), ang e-commerce tiers (5.5.b at 5.5.c), ang Php 130.00 Export Processing Charge (5.6), ang Php 140.00 Balikbayan Box charge (5.3), ang Php 310.00 Returning Resident charge (5.4), ang Php 4,500.00 Aircraft Supervision Fee (4.2), at ang AEO fees sa 4.4 at 5.12. Alamin din kung sino ang magbabayad ng bawat fee (shipping line, airline, importer, exporter, CBW o CFW operator, third party provider).

❓ Madalas Malito ang Students: Tanong: Pareho ba ang AEO Annual Supervision Fee (4.4) at AEO Application Charge (5.12)?
Sagot: Hindi. Ang 4.4 ay taunang bayad para sa field monitoring at validation ng status (Micro Php 0.00 hanggang Large Php 36,000.00) at napupunta sa Trust Fund. Ang 5.12 ay application charge (Micro Php 1,500.00 hanggang Large Php 10,000.00) at napupunta sa General Fund.

🔗 Related Topics: CMTA Sec. 204, 1211, 1300, 1301, at 1508. CAO 12-2019 (transshipment). CAO 01-2018 (Balikbayan Box). CAO 06-2016 (Returning Resident). EO No. 635, s. 2007 (Container Security). CAO 01-2025 (Cross-Border e-Commerce). CMO 16-2023 (Duty Drawback processing fee).

paragraphs.text: This CAO implements Section 204 Chapter 1, Title II; Section 1211, Chapter 2, Title XII; Section 1300, Title XIII; Section 1301, Title XIII; and Section 1508, Title XV of Republic Act (RA) No. 10863, otherwise known as the Customs Modernization and Tariff Act (CMTA).

ai.title: Introduction: Batas na Ipinapatupad
ai.content:
📖 Kahulugan: Ipinapatupad ng CAO na ito ang Sec. 204 (Chapter 1, Title II); Sec. 1211 (Chapter 2, Title XII); Sec. 1300 at Sec. 1301 (Title XIII); at Sec. 1508 (Title XV) ng RA No. 10863 o Customs Modernization and Tariff Act (CMTA).

💡 Simpleng Paliwanag: Ito ang legal na pinagmumulan ng CAO. Ang CAO ay implementing rules lang; ang CMTA ang pinagbabatayan ng kapangyarihan ng BOC na maningil ng fees, dues, at charges.

⚠️ Dapat Tandaan: Limang CMTA sections ang nakalista: 204, 1211, 1300, 1301, at 1508. Kapag tinanong kung anong batas ang ipinapatupad, RA No. 10863 (CMTA) ang sagot.

paragraphs.text: This CAO covers all Service Fees, Dues, and Charges collected by the Bureau of Customs from the Shipping Lines, Airlines, Air Express Operators, Importers, Exporters, Customs Brokers, Freight Forwarders, Consolidators, Deconsolidators, Logistics Providers, Transhippers, Operators of Customs Bonded Warehouses and other Customs Facilities and Warehouses, Free Zone Locators or registered enterprises, Third Party Solutions Providers, and all other parties served by the Bureau.

ai.title: Scope ng CAO
ai.content:
📖 Kahulugan: Sakop ng CAO ang lahat ng Service Fees, Dues, at Charges na kinokolekta ng BOC mula sa mga nakalistang stakeholders, kabilang ang shipping lines, airlines, air express operators, importers, exporters, customs brokers, freight forwarders, consolidators, deconsolidators, logistics providers, transhippers, operators ng customs bonded warehouses at ibang customs facilities, free zone locators o registered enterprises, third party solutions providers, at lahat ng iba pang pinagsisilbihan ng Bureau.

💡 Simpleng Paliwanag: Halos lahat ng may transaksyon sa BOC ay sakop. May 'catch-all' din sa dulo: 'all other parties served by the Bureau'.

⚠️ Dapat Tandaan: Hindi lang importers at exporters ang sakop. Pati airlines, shipping lines, brokers, warehouse operators, free zone locators, at third party solutions providers.

paragraphs.text: Consolidators — shall refer to a foreign-registered forwarding company acting as a Non-Vessel Operating Common Carrier (NVOCC) which procures the transport of goods by sea or air and issues in its name house bills of lading (HBLs) or house airway bills (HAWBs) to consignors of shipments under its solicitation, to whom it directly assumes the liabilities and responsibilities of a common carrier for the transportation of such goods from the point of receipt to the point of destination of such goods, and ships the shipments together in its name under a master bill of lading (MBL) or master airway bill (MAWB) consigned to its Deconsolidator at the port of destination in the Philippines.

ai.title: Consolidators
ai.content:
📖 Kahulugan: Foreign-registered forwarding company na nagsisilbing NVOCC, na nag-aayos ng transport ng goods sa dagat o himpapawid at nag-iisyu sa sarili nitong pangalan ng house bills of lading (HBL) o house airway bills (HAWB), at nagpapadala ng shipments nang sama-sama sa ilalim ng master bill of lading (MBL) o master airway bill (MAWB) na naka-consign sa Deconsolidator nito sa port of destination sa Pilipinas.

💡 Simpleng Paliwanag: Sila ang nag-iipon ng maliliit na shipments sa isang malaking shipment. Dayuhang kumpanya ito, at ang Deconsolidator nila sa Pilipinas ang tatanggap.

⚠️ Dapat Tandaan: Mahalagang pagkakaiba: Consolidator = foreign-registered. Deconsolidator = local. Lumalabas ang Consolidator sa 5.5.b (e-commerce goods).

ai.title: Customs Broker
ai.content:
📖 Kahulugan: Taong bona fide holder ng valid na Certificate of Registration o Professional Identification Card na inisyu ng Professional Regulatory Board at Professional Regulation Commission ayon sa RA No. 9280 (Customs Brokers Act of 2004).

💡 Simpleng Paliwanag: Lisensyadong customs broker. Hindi sapat ang basta nagpoproseso ng entry; dapat may valid na lisensya.

⚠️ Dapat Tandaan: May Registration Charge para sa Customs Broker (5.21) at GPP (5.22). Legal basis: RA No. 9280.

paragraphs.text: Customs Facilities and Warehouses (CFW) — shall refer to facilities for temporary storage of goods established and authorized by the Bureau pursuant to Title VIII, Chapter 2 of the CMTA and classified according to the categories based on total assets. These include container yards, container freight stations, seaport temporary storage warehouses, airport temporary storage warehouses and other premises for customs purposes.

ai.title: Customs Facilities and Warehouses (CFW)
ai.content:
📖 Kahulugan: Mga pasilidad para sa temporary storage ng goods na itinatag at pinahintulutan ng Bureau ayon sa Title VIII, Chapter 2 ng CMTA, at inuuri ayon sa categories batay sa total assets. Kasama ang container yards, container freight stations, seaport at airport temporary storage warehouses, at iba pang premises para sa customs purposes.

💡 Simpleng Paliwanag: Mga temporary storage ng goods na hawak ng Bureau authority: yard, CFS, at warehouses sa port at airport.

⚠️ Dapat Tandaan: Hindi ito pareho ng CBW. CFW = temporary storage. CBW = bonded, duty-free storage. May CFW Fee (4.11) at CFW Annual Supervision Charge (5.32).

paragraphs.text: Customs Services — shall refer to work performed by customs personnel outside of his/her Official Work Station, or Overtime Work performed for the benefit of concerned stakeholders, such as customs boarding formalities on Vessels and Aircrafts, baggage clearance of international passengers, supervision of loading and unloading of cargoes from Vessels and Aircrafts, Under Guarding of goods for transit/transfer, clearance of goods covered by different types of declaration and other related services.

ai.title: Customs Services
ai.content:
📖 Kahulugan: Trabahong ginawa ng customs personnel sa labas ng Official Work Station, o Overtime Work para sa kapakinabangan ng stakeholders, tulad ng boarding formalities sa Vessels at Aircrafts, baggage clearance ng international passengers, supervision ng loading at unloading ng cargoes, Under Guarding ng goods para sa transit o transfer, clearance ng goods na sakop ng iba't ibang uri ng declaration, at iba pang related services.

💡 Simpleng Paliwanag: Ito ang 'serbisyong may bayad': kapag lumabas ng official station o nag-overtime ang Customs personnel para sa stakeholder.

⚠️ Dapat Tandaan: Dalawang test: (1) sa labas ng Official Work Station, o (2) overtime. Ito ang basehan ng Service Fees sa Sec. 4.
ai.prompt: Ipaliwanag nang simple sa Taglish ang Sec. 3.9 ng CAO 02-2024 (Customs Services), na parang customs review mentor ka. paragraphs.text: Deconsolidator — shall refer to a local Freight Forwarder or Consolidator's agent that provides services to ungroup or deconsolidate shipments, orders, goods, etc. to facilitate their distribution.

ai.title: Deconsolidator
ai.content:
📖 Kahulugan: Local Freight Forwarder o agent ng Consolidator na nagbubukod-bukod (deconsolidate) ng shipments, orders, goods, at iba pa para mapadali ang distribution.

💡 Simpleng Paliwanag: Siya ang tumatanggap ng consolidated shipment sa Pilipinas at naghihiwa-hiwalay nito.

⚠️ Dapat Tandaan: Local ang Deconsolidator. Ito ang consignee ng MBL o MAWB mula sa Consolidator (3.5).

paragraphs.text: Electronic Commerce (E-Commerce) – shall refer to the sale or purchase of goods and services, whether between businesses, households, individuals, governments, and other public or private organizations, conducted over computer-mediated networks. The goods and services are ordered over those networks, but the payment and the ultimate delivery of the goods or service may be conducted on or offline.

ai.title: Electronic Commerce (E-Commerce)
ai.content:
📖 Kahulugan: Pagbebenta o pagbili ng goods at services, sa pagitan man ng businesses, households, individuals, governments, at ibang public o private organizations, sa pamamagitan ng computer-mediated networks. Online ang order, pero puwedeng online o offline ang bayad at delivery.

💡 Simpleng Paliwanag: Ang importante ay online ang pag-order. Ang bayad at delivery ay puwedeng online o offline.

⚠️ Dapat Tandaan: Ito ang batayan ng special rates para sa cross-border e-commerce goods sa 5.5.b at 5.5.c.

paragraphs.text: Exporter — shall refer to a natural or juridical person engaged in the export of any goods or commodities to a foreign country from the Philippines.

💡 Simpleng Paliwanag: Individual o kumpanyang nag-e-export mula Pilipinas.

⚠️ Dapat Tandaan: Nagbabayad ng Export Processing Charge (5.6), Advance Ruling (5.17), at Certificate of Origin Processing Charge (5.29).

paragraphs.text: Free Zone Locator — shall refer to a sole proprietorship, partnership, corporation or entity duly registered with the Free Zone Authority and issued a Certificate of Registration and/or Tax Exemption that is not expired or has not been revoked, suspended or cancelled.

ai.title: Free Zone Locator
ai.content:
📖 Kahulugan: Sole proprietorship, partnership, corporation, o entity na maayos na nakarehistro sa Free Zone Authority at binigyan ng Certificate of Registration at/o Tax Exemption na hindi expired at hindi na-revoke, na-suspend, o na-cancel.

💡 Simpleng Paliwanag: Negosyong nasa loob ng free zone na may valid na registration. Kapag expired o na-revoke, hindi na siya 'locator' ayon sa CAO.

⚠️ Dapat Tandaan: Ang Free Zone Locator ang nagbabayad ng Supervision Fee sa 4.3 para sa underguarding services.

paragraphs.text: Freight Forwarder — shall refer to a local entity that acts as a cargo intermediary and facilitates transport of goods on behalf of its clients without assuming the role of a carrier, which also performs other forwarding services, such as booking cargo space, negotiating freight rates, preparing documents, advancing freight payment, providing, packing or crating, trucking and warehousing, engaging as an agent or as a representative of a foreign NVOCC or cargo Consolidator named in an MBL as consignee of a consolidated shipment, and other related undertakings.

ai.title: Freight Forwarder
ai.content:
📖 Kahulugan: Local entity na nagsisilbing cargo intermediary at nagpapadali ng transport ng goods para sa mga kliyente nang hindi nagiging carrier. Kasama sa trabaho ang booking ng cargo space, negosasyon ng freight rates, paghahanda ng documents, pag-advance ng freight payment, packing o crating, trucking, warehousing, at pagiging agent ng foreign NVOCC o Consolidator na nakapangalan bilang consignee sa MBL.

💡 Simpleng Paliwanag: Siya ang 'tagapag-ayos' ng shipment ng kliyente. Hindi siya ang carrier.

⚠️ Dapat Tandaan: Local entity ito, hindi katulad ng Consolidator na foreign-registered. Makikita siya sa 4.5 at 5.5.b.

💡 Simpleng Paliwanag: Individual o kumpanyang nag-i-import.

paragraphs.text: Logistics Provider — shall refer to a company that provides management over the flow of goods and materials between the point of origin to end-use destination. The provider will often handle shipping, inventory, warehousing, packaging, and security functions of the shipments.

ai.title: Logistics Provider
ai.content:
📖 Kahulugan: Kumpanyang namamahala sa daloy ng goods at materials mula point of origin hanggang end-use destination. Madalas itong humahawak ng shipping, inventory, warehousing, packaging, at security ng shipments.

💡 Simpleng Paliwanag: End-to-end na tagapamahala ng galaw ng goods.

⚠️ Dapat Tandaan: Isa ito sa mga nakalistang stakeholders sa Scope.

paragraphs.text: Manufacturing Customs Bonded Warehouse (MCBW) – it is a warehouse established for the manufacture of products utilizing raw materials or components that are imported duty and tax-free conditioned on the exportation of the finished products within the period prescribed herein or withdrawal for domestic consumption upon payment of duties and tax.

ai.title: Manufacturing Customs Bonded Warehouse (MCBW)
ai.content:
📖 Kahulugan: Warehouse na itinatag para sa paggawa ng products gamit ang raw materials o components na na-import nang duty at tax-free, kondisyon na ie-export ang finished products sa loob ng prescribed period, o i-withdraw para sa domestic consumption sa pagbabayad ng duties at tax.

💡 Simpleng Paliwanag: Bonded warehouse na gumagawa ng produkto. Duty-free ang materials basta ie-export ang finished goods o babayaran ang duties kung ilalabas sa lokal.

⚠️ Dapat Tandaan: Manufacturing ito. Ihambing sa NCBW (3.18) na storage lang.

paragraphs.text: Non-Manufacturing Customs Bonded Warehouse (NCBW) – it is a warehouse where goods are stored duty-and-tax-free conditioned on the eventual withdrawal of the goods for consumption and shall only be withdrawn within the period prescribed upon payment of the corresponding duties, taxes, and other charges whether or not the goods are in the same state as imported.

ai.title: Non-Manufacturing Customs Bonded Warehouse (NCBW)
ai.content:
📖 Kahulugan: Warehouse kung saan duty-and-tax-free na nakaimbak ang goods, kondisyon na i-wi-withdraw ito para sa consumption sa loob ng prescribed period at sa pagbabayad ng kaukulang duties, taxes, at charges, nasa parehong estado man o hindi gaya ng na-import.

💡 Simpleng Paliwanag: Bonded warehouse para sa storage lang. Walang manufacturing.

⚠️ Dapat Tandaan: Non-manufacturing ito. Ihambing sa MCBW (3.17).

ai.content:

paragraphs.text: Port of Entry — shall refer to a domestic port open to both domestic and international trade, including principal ports of entry and subports of entry. A principal Port of Entry is the chief Port of Entry of the Customs District wherein it is situated and is the permanent station of the District Collector of such port. Subports of entry are under the administrative jurisdiction of the District Collector of the principal Port of Entry of the Customs District. Port of Entry as used in this CAO shall include airport of entry.

ai.title: Port of Entry
ai.content:
📖 Kahulugan: Domestic port na bukas sa domestic at international trade, kasama ang principal ports of entry at subports of entry. Ang principal Port of Entry ay ang chief port ng Customs District at ang permanent station ng District Collector. Ang subports ay nasa administrative jurisdiction ng District Collector ng principal Port of Entry. Kasama rin dito ang airport of entry.

💡 Simpleng Paliwanag: Pangunahing pantalan o paliparan ng isang Customs District, kasama ang mga subports nito.

⚠️ Dapat Tandaan: Dito pumapasok ang Vessel Supervision Fee (4.1). Sa CAO na ito, kasama sa 'Port of Entry' ang airport of entry.

ai.title: Third Party Service Provider

💡 Simpleng Paliwanag: Malawak ang kahulugan: hindi lang malalaking barko.

paragraphs.text: Warehouse Operator — shall refer to a private entity authorized by government to offer services of receiving, handling, and checking as well as the custody and delivery of conventional, breakbulk or stripped or stuffed containerized foreign cargo over piers or wharves, in transit sheds or warehouses and open storage areas. For purposes of this Order and as used herein Warehouse Operator shall refer to operators of CBW's and CFW's.

ai.title: Warehouse Operator
ai.content:
📖 Kahulugan: Pribadong entity na pinahintulutan ng gobyerno na magbigay ng services sa pagtanggap, paghawak, at pag-check, pati ang custody at delivery, ng conventional, breakbulk, o stripped/stuffed containerized foreign cargo sa piers, wharves, transit sheds, warehouses, at open storage areas. Sa CAO na ito, tumutukoy ito sa operators ng CBW at CFW.

💡 Simpleng Paliwanag: Sa CAO na ito, 'warehouse operator' = operator ng CBW o CFW.

⚠️ Dapat Tandaan: Sila ang nagbabayad ng Annual Supervision Charges (5.31 at 5.32) at ng CFW Fee (4.11).

paragraphs.text: The following Fees shall be collected and shall accrue to the Trust Fund which may be used for payment of allowances and overtime services for Customs personnel:

ai.title: Customs Service Fee: Intro
ai.content:
📖 Kahulugan: Intro ng Section 4. Ang mga Fee sa ilalim nito ay kokolektahin at mapupunta sa Trust Fund, na puwedeng gamitin para sa pagbabayad ng allowances at overtime services ng Customs personnel.

💡 Simpleng Paliwanag: Ito ang pangunahing pagkakaiba ng Sec. 4 at Sec. 5. Ang Sec. 4 (Service Fees) ay Trust Fund para sa allowances at overtime ng Customs personnel. Ang Sec. 5 (Dues and Charges) ay General Fund.

⚠️ Dapat Tandaan: Trust Fund = Sec. 4. General Fund = Sec. 5. Kabisaduhin ito; madalas itanong sa exam.
ai.prompt: Ipaliwanag nang simple sa Taglish ang Section 4 (intro) ng CAO 02-2024 (Customs Service Fee: Intro), na parang customs review mentor ka. Sec. 3.9, Sec. 5, Sec. 7), at linawin ang mga karaniwang maling akala ng students. Huwag mag-imbento ng rates, penalties, o requirements na wala sa text.

paragraphs.text:
Vessel Supervision Fee – shall be paid by the shipping line or its agent for every Vessel engaged in foreign commerce that enters and clears from a Port of Entry and where Customs Services are rendered such as the Tagging of Estimated Time of Arrival (ETA) and Actual Time of Arrival (ATA); Conduct of Boarding Formalities; Issuance of Entrance and Clearance Permits; Supervision during Unloading and Loading of Cargoes and empty containers, including shifting of containers during bunkering, and rendering of chandling services during discharging of sludge; Supervision during emergency situations, for medical purposes, sheltering, repair, and other related services.
Boarding Formalities per vessel | Php 2,250.00
Entrance and Clearance per day | Php 1,087.00
Loading and Unloading per day | Php 4,500.00
Supervision fee for bunkering and other emergency purposes like medical, sheltering, repair, marine accidents, dockyard lay-up and others. | Php 2,250.00

ai.title: 4.1 Vessel Supervision Fee
ai.content:
📖 Kahulugan: Babayaran ng shipping line o agent nito para sa bawat Vessel na nasa foreign commerce at pumapasok at lumalabas sa isang Port of Entry kung saan may Customs Services, tulad ng pag-tag ng ETA at ATA, boarding formalities, pag-isyu ng entrance at clearance permits, supervision sa loading at unloading, at supervision sa emergency situations. Rates: Boarding Formalities Php 2,250.00 per vessel; Entrance and Clearance Php 1,087.00 per day; Loading and Unloading Php 4,500.00 per day; Bunkering at ibang emergency purposes (medical, sheltering, repair, marine accidents, dockyard lay-up, at iba pa) Php 2,250.00.

💡 Simpleng Paliwanag: Bayad ito ng shipping line sa serbisyo ng Customs para sa barko. May apat na component, at dalawa sa mga ito ay per day.

📦 Halimbawa: Kung 2 araw ang loading at unloading ng isang vessel, ang bahagi lang na iyon ay Php 4,500 x 2 = Php 9,000. Dagdag pa rito ang boarding at ang entrance and clearance fee.

⚠️ Dapat Tandaan: Apat na rates: Php 2,250 (boarding, per vessel), Php 1,087 (entrance and clearance, per day), Php 4,500 (loading at unloading, per day), Php 2,250 (bunkering at emergency purposes). Trust Fund ito.
ai.prompt: Ipaliwanag nang simple sa Taglish ang Sec. 4.1 ng CAO 02-2024 (4.1 Vessel Supervision Fee), na parang customs review mentor ka. Sec. 3.21, 3.23, 3.20), at linawin ang mga karaniwang maling akala ng students. Huwag mag-imbento ng rates, penalties, o requirements na wala sa text.

paragraphs.text: Aircraft Supervision Fee – An Aircraft Supervison Fee of Php 4,500.00 shall be paid by the Airline or its agent for every Aircraft engaged in foreign commerce that landed and departed from an international airport of entry and where Customs Services are rendered such as the Tagging of ETA and ATA; Issuance of entrance and clearance permits; Conduct of boarding formalities; Supervision of the loading and unloading of cargoes; Under guarding of cargoes and Aircrafts; Clearance of passengers and baggage; Storage and release of held baggage and other related services.

ai.title: 4.2 Aircraft Supervision Fee

ai.title: CAO 01-2022: Customs Bonded Warehouses
ai.content:
📖 Kahulugan: Ang CAO 01-2022 ang master rulebook para sa lahat ng Customs Bonded Warehouses (CBWs): mga bodega kung saan puwedeng ilagay ang imported goods nang duty and tax free habang nasa bond, basta masunod ang kondisyon (i-export ang finished products o bayaran ang duties kapag para sa local consumption). Ini-implement nito ang CMTA Secs. 301, 303 at 801 hanggang 813, at pinagsama nito ang lahat ng lumang CAOs sa CBWs.

🔍 Breakdown: Sec. 1-2 Scope at Objectives; Sec. 3 Definitions; Sec. 4 General Provisions (types ng CBW, terms and conditions, pre-operation requirements); Sec. 5 Administrative Provisions (application, renewal, structural changes, extension warehouse, relocation); Sec. 6 Membership sa CCBW; Sec. 7 Appeals; Sec. 8 Operational Provisions (goods declaration, transfer, storage period, liquidation); Sec. 9-10 Responsibilities at Liabilities ng operator; Sec. 11 Suspension at Closure; Sec. 12-13 Inspection at Audit; Sec. 14 Supervision Fees; Sec. 15 Penalties; Sec. 16-21 IRR, Periodic Review, Transitory, Separability, Repealing at Effectivity.

💡 Simpleng Paliwanag: Isipin mo ang CBW bilang 'bonded' na bodega na laging binabantayan ng Bureau. Hindi muna binabayaran ang buwis sa imported raw materials, pero kapag na-export ang finished products sa tamang panahon, 'liquidated' na ang entry at na-cancel ang bond. Kapag hindi, may bayad at penalties.

📦 Halimbawa: Ang isang garment manufacturer ay nag-import ng tela na bonded sa kanyang MCBW. Ginawa niyang damit at na-export sa loob ng one (1) year mula arrival. Nag-submit siya ng liquidation documents sa loob ng 60 days mula complete exportation kaya na-cancel ang bond at walang duties na binayaran.

⭐ Bakit Mahalaga Ito? Ito ang pangunahing rules para sa warehousing operations. Pinoprotektahan nito ang revenue ng gobyerno habang sinusuportahan ang export industries.

⚠️ Dapat Tandaan: Ang Authority to Operate ay valid ng 3 taon at hindi transferable. Ang storage period ay 1 year (3 months para sa perishable goods). May fixed na supervision fees at penalties.

🎯 Board Exam Tip: Memorize ang validity (3 taon), ang renewal window (hindi lalampas ng 90 days pero hindi mas maaga sa 120 days bago mag-expire), ang CCBW membership (3 hanggang 30 members, projected duties hindi lalampas ng PhP300M) at ang penalty ladder sa Sec. 15.

❓ Madalas Malito ang Students: Tanong: Pareho ba ang MCBW at CCBW? Sagot: Hindi. Ang MCBW ay umbrella type na kasama ang MMBW, GTMBW, CCBW at ICBW. Ang CCBW ay shared bonded warehouse na may accredited members.

🔗 Related Topics: CMTA Title VIII (Warehousing), CMTA Secs. 1422, 1430 at 1431, CAO 9-2019, CMO 39-2008 (CPRS).

paragraphs.text: This Customs Administrative Order (CAO) implements Sections 301 and 303, Chapter 2, Title III, and Sections 801 to 813, Chapter 2, Title VIII, in relation to Section 204 and other relevant sections of Republic Act No. 10863, otherwise known as the Customs Modernization and Tariff Act (CMTA), and consolidates all existing CAOs dealing on Customs Bonded Warehouses (CBWs).

ai.title: Legal Basis ng CAO
ai.content:
📖 Kahulugan: Sinasabi dito kung saang batas nakabase ang CAO: CMTA (RA 10863) Secs. 301, 303 at 801 hanggang 813, kaugnay ng Sec. 204. Pinagsasama rin nito ang lahat ng lumang CAOs sa CBWs.

💡 Simpleng Paliwanag: Isang rulebook na lang para sa CBWs, hindi mo na kailangang halukayin ang maraming lumang CAOs.

⚠️ Dapat Tandaan: Implementing rule lang ito; ang CMTA pa rin ang mas mataas na batas.

paragraphs.text: This CAO applies to all types of CBWs listed in the CMTA and those that may be created by the Secretary of Finance, upon the recommendation of the Commissioner pursuant to Section 803 of the CMTA.

ai.title: Scope ng CAO
ai.content:
📖 Kahulugan: Sakop nito ang lahat ng uri ng CBW na nasa CMTA, pati ang mga bagong uri na likhain ng Secretary of Finance sa rekomendasyon ng Commissioner (CMTA Sec. 803).

💡 Simpleng Paliwanag: Kahit anong klase ng bonded warehouse, sakop ng CAO na ito, kasama ang mga future types.

⚠️ Dapat Tandaan: Ang Secretary of Finance ang may kapangyarihang lumikha ng bagong uri, hindi ang District Collector.

paragraphs.text: To provide the guidelines for the establishment, operation, supervision and control of CBWs;

ai.title: Objective: Guidelines
ai.content:
📖 Kahulugan: Unang layunin ng CAO ang magtakda ng guidelines sa pagtatayo, pagpapatakbo, supervision at control ng CBWs.

💡 Simpleng Paliwanag: Ito ang 'paano magtayo, paano patakbuhin, at paano babantayan' ng bonded warehouses.

paragraphs.text: To protect revenue through the institution of safeguard and control measures over CBWs;

ai.title: Objective: Revenue Protection
ai.content:
📖 Kahulugan: Layunin nitong protektahan ang kita ng gobyerno gamit ang safeguards at control measures sa CBWs.

💡 Simpleng Paliwanag: Dahil walang binabayarang buwis sa bonded goods, kailangang mahigpit ang bantay para hindi ito mapunta sa lokal na merkado nang walang bayad.

paragraphs.text: To define the rights and corresponding obligations of operators of CBWs accredited sub-contractors and members;

ai.title: Objective: Rights and Obligations
ai.content:
📖 Kahulugan: Nililinaw dito ang karapatan at obligasyon ng CBW operators, accredited sub-contractors at members.

💡 Simpleng Paliwanag: Alam ng bawat player kung ano ang puwede at hindi puwede nilang gawin, at kung ano ang pananagutan nila sa Bureau.

paragraphs.text: To improve the level of compliance of CBW operators with customs warehousing laws and regulations and provide penalties for non-compliance;

ai.title: Objective: Compliance
ai.content:
📖 Kahulugan: Layunin nitong pataasin ang compliance ng CBW operators sa warehousing laws at magtakda ng penalties sa lalabag.

💡 Simpleng Paliwanag: May 'pangil' ang rules dahil may kaakibat na parusa, at ito ang laman ng Sec. 15.

⚠️ Dapat Tandaan: Konektado ito sa Compliance Rate System (CRS) sa Sec. 3.18 at 4.11.5.

paragraphs.text: To establish, develop and implement a CBW raw materials management system making full use of information and communications technology and more transparent procedures which would aid the Bureau in the monitoring, supervision and control of CBW operations; and

ai.title: Objective: ICT-Based Raw Materials System
ai.content:
📖 Kahulugan: Layunin nitong magtayo at gumamit ng raw materials management system na ICT-based at transparent para matulungan ang Bureau sa monitoring, supervision at control ng CBW operations.

💡 Simpleng Paliwanag: Automated na ang pagbabantay (hindi na puro papel), at dito galing ang AIMS, ABMS, RMLS at WVDB sa definitions.

⚠️ Dapat Tandaan: Ang 'and' sa dulo ay connector papunta sa huling objective (2.6).

paragraphs.text: To align Customs regulations on CBWs with international standards and best practices.

ai.title: Objective: International Standards
ai.content:
📖 Kahulugan: Layunin nitong iayon ang CBW regulations sa international standards at best practices.

💡 Simpleng Paliwanag: Hindi dapat naiiwan ang Pilipinas sa global customs practices, para competitive ang exporters natin.

paragraphs.text: For purposes of this CAO, the following terms are defined accordingly:

ai.title: Intro sa Definitions
ai.content:
📖 Kahulugan: Panimulang pangungusap na nagsasabing ang mga sumusunod na termino ay may eksaktong kahulugan para sa CAO na ito lamang.

💡 Simpleng Paliwanag: Kapag may conflict sa pang-araw-araw na gamit ng salita, ang definition dito ang masusunod pagdating sa CBW rules.

⚠️ Dapat Tandaan: Madalas lumabas sa exam ang mga definition, kaya basahin nang mabuti ang eksaktong wording.

paragraphs.text: Accessories — shall refer to goods which are neither raw materials nor supplies which enhance the finished products to be exported.

ai.title: Accessories
ai.content:
📖 Kahulugan: Goods na hindi raw materials at hindi rin supplies, pero nagpapaganda o nagko-complete sa finished product na ie-export.

💡 Simpleng Paliwanag: Parang butones, zipper o label sa garments. Hindi sila ang mismong tela, pero kasama sa final product.

⚠️ Dapat Tandaan: Iba ito sa 'supplies' (3.45) na pang-maintenance lang at hindi kasama sa FOM.

paragraphs.text: Accountable Officer — shall refer to a responsible official of the CBW named and designated by the operator as the person, other than himself, answerable and liable to the Bureau for all the operational aspects of the warehouse.

ai.title: Accountable Officer
ai.content:
📖 Kahulugan: Responsableng opisyal ng CBW na itinalaga ng operator, hindi ang operator mismo, na sasagot at mananagot sa Bureau sa lahat ng operational aspects ng bodega.

💡 Simpleng Paliwanag: Siya ang 'point person' ng Bureau sa araw-araw na operasyon.

⚠️ Dapat Tandaan: Ibang tao siya sa operator, pero liable pa rin siya sa Bureau.

paragraphs.text: Accredited Client/End-User — shall refer to a natural or juridical person authorized by the Bureau to be a client/end-user of Industry-specific CBW (ICBW).

ai.title: Accredited Client/End-User
ai.content:
📖 Kahulugan: Taong natural o juridical na pinahintulutan ng Bureau na maging client/end-user ng Industry-Specific CBW (ICBW).

💡 Simpleng Paliwanag: Siya ang tumatanggap at gumagamit ng goods mula sa ICBW, tulad ng airline na kliyente ng airline CBW.

⚠️ Dapat Tandaan: Ang 'client/end-user' ay para sa ICBW, samantalang ang 'member' ay para sa CCBW.

paragraphs.text: Accredited Client-Exporter — shall refer to client-exporters accredited by the Bureau to receive finished goods manufactured by MCBWs to be used in their registered export activities.

ai.content:
📖 Kahulugan: Client-exporters na accredited ng Bureau para tumanggap ng finished goods na gawa ng MCBWs para sa kanilang registered export activities.

💡 Simpleng Paliwanag: Ang MCBW ang gumagawa, at ang Client-Exporter ang tatanggap at mag-e-export.

⚠️ Dapat Tandaan: Kailangang accredited siya ng Bureau bago makatanggap ng bonded finished goods.

paragraphs.text: Airlines Customs Bonded Warehouse and Airlines Catering Customs Bonded Warehouse — shall refer to an Industry-Specific Customs Bonded Warehouses (ICBW) where supplies, spare parts, in-flight duty-free items and such other goods necessary for the reasonable requirements of the aircraft, its crew and passengers are stored.

ai.title: Airlines CBW and Airlines Catering CBW
ai.content:
📖 Kahulugan: Mga ICBW kung saan nakaimbak ang supplies, spare parts, in-flight duty-free items at iba pang goods na kailangan ng aircraft, crew at pasahero.

💡 Simpleng Paliwanag: Ito ang bonded na bodega ng airlines para sa spare parts, pagkain at duty-free items sa eroplano.

⚠️ Dapat Tandaan: Ayon sa 4.3.2(d), ang mga dating Airlines CBW at Airlines Catering CBW ay re-classified bilang ICBW.

paragraphs.text: Alert Order — shall refer to a written Order issued by the Commissioner, District Collector, or other customs officers authorized in writing by the Commissioner after the Lodgement of Goods Declaration and before their actual release from customs custody, on the basis of derogatory information regarding possible non-compliance with the CMTA and other laws, rules and regulations enforced by the Bureau.

ai.title: Alert Order
ai.content:
📖 Kahulugan: Written order ng Commissioner, District Collector o awtorisadong customs officer, inilalabas pagkatapos ng Lodgement ng Goods Declaration at bago ma-release ang goods, base sa derogatory information tungkol sa posibleng non-compliance.

💡 Simpleng Paliwanag: Parang 'hold' sa shipment habang may pinag-aaralang red flag.

⚠️ Dapat Tandaan: Sa Sec. 8.2, kapag ang goods ay nasa Alert Order, hindi ito agad mati-transfer sa CBW.

paragraphs.text: Authority to Operate — shall refer to the authority given by the Bureau allowing persons, natural or juridical, to establish and operate a CBW.

ai.title: Authority to Operate
ai.content:
📖 Kahulugan: Awtoridad mula sa Bureau na nagpapahintulot sa natural o juridical person na magtayo at mag-operate ng CBW.

💡 Simpleng Paliwanag: Ito ang 'lisensya' mo. Walang Authority, hindi ka puwedeng mag-bonded warehouse.

⚠️ Dapat Tandaan: Personal ito at hindi transferable (4.6), at ang pag-operate nang wala nito ay may bar sa warehousing privileges (4.9).

paragraphs.text: Authority to Transfer or Sell (ATS) — shall refer to the document issued by the District Collector allowing transfer or sale of imported raw materials, semi-finished products, or finished products to another CBW, Client-Exporter, Client/End-User, or Freeport Zone locator for subsequent export. Transfers to sub-contractors or members of CCBW shall be covered by Authority to Transfer only.

ai.title: Authority to Transfer or Sell (ATS)
ai.content:
📖 Kahulugan: Dokumentong inilalabas ng District Collector na nagpapahintulot ng transfer o sale ng imported raw materials, semi-finished o finished products sa ibang CBW, Client-Exporter, Client/End-User o Freeport Zone locator para sa subsequent export.

💡 Simpleng Paliwanag: Hindi puwedeng basta ipasa o ibenta ang bonded goods; kailangan ng ATS mula sa District Collector.

⚠️ Dapat Tandaan: Sa sub-contractors o members ng CCBW, Authority to Transfer lang ang sakop.

paragraphs.text: Automated Inventory Management System (AIMS) —shall refer to the automated system to be adopted by the CBW operator as a tool to determine and monitor the stock inventory of imported raw materials from the time of its entry into the CBW up to liquidation of the covering warehousing entry.

ai.title: AIMS
ai.content:
📖 Kahulugan: Automated system na gagamitin ng CBW operator para malaman at ma-monitor ang stock inventory ng imported raw materials mula pagpasok sa CBW hanggang sa liquidation ng warehousing entry.

💡 Simpleng Paliwanag: Digital na 'stock card' ng operator, bawat sako, roll o piraso ay may bakas.

⚠️ Dapat Tandaan: Ang AIMS ay para sa operator, samantalang ang ABMS (3.10) ay para sa Bureau. Tingnan din ang 4.13.2.
ai.prompt: Ipaliwanag nang simple ang Sec. 3.9 ng CAO 01-2022 tungkol sa Automated Inventory Management System (AIMS). Magbigay ng practical customs example, ipaliwanag kung bakit ito umiiral, banggitin ang related provisions, at linawin ang common misconceptions.

paragraphs.text: Automated Bonds Management System (ABMS) — shall refer to the automated system to be utilized by the Bureau as a tool in the effective monitoring and cancellation of bonds for the liquidation of raw materials/entries.

ai.title: ABMS
ai.content:
📖 Kahulugan: Automated system ng Bureau para sa monitoring at cancellation ng bonds kapag na-liquidate na ang raw materials/entries.

💡 Simpleng Paliwanag: Ito ang 'bond tracker' ng Bureau. Kapag kumpleto ang liquidation, na-cancel ang bond.

⚠️ Dapat Tandaan: Ginagamit din ito sa automatic debiting ng assessed duties at taxes sa Bond Account (4.12.9).
ai.prompt: Ipaliwanag nang simple ang Sec. 3.10 ng CAO 01-2022 tungkol sa Automated Bonds Management System (ABMS). Magbigay ng practical customs example, ipaliwanag kung bakit ito umiiral, banggitin ang related provisions, at linawin ang common misconceptions.

paragraphs.text: Bureau — shall refer to the Bureau of Customs.

ai.title: Bureau
ai.content:
📖 Kahulugan: Ang 'Bureau' sa buong CAO ay ang Bureau of Customs.

💡 Simpleng Paliwanag: Kapag nabasa mo ang 'Bureau', BOC ang tinutukoy, hindi DOF o ibang ahensya.
ai.prompt: Ipaliwanag nang simple ang Sec. 3.11 ng CAO 01-2022 tungkol sa kahulugan ng Bureau. Magbigay ng practical customs example, ipaliwanag kung bakit ito umiiral, banggitin ang related provisions, at linawin ang common misconceptions.

paragraphs.text: Certificate of Authority to Operate — shall refer to the document signed by the Commissioner of Customs and issued by the Bureau to persons, natural or juridical, duly authorized to operate a CBW, to be an accredited member, accredited subcontractor or accredited client/end-user stating its name, authority (license) number, exact office and warehouse address, date of grant and expiry of authority and type of the approved warehouse, renewable every three (3) years, after proper re-evaluation and favorable recommendation by the CBWC.

ai.title: Certificate of Authority to Operate
ai.content:
📖 Kahulugan: Dokumentong pinirmahan ng Commissioner at inisyu ng Bureau sa mga awtorisadong mag-operate ng CBW o maging accredited member, subcontractor o client/end-user. Nakasaad dito ang pangalan, license number, address, petsa ng grant at expiry, at uri ng warehouse. Renewable ito kada tatlong (3) taon pagkatapos ng re-evaluation at favorable recommendation ng CBWC.

💡 Simpleng Paliwanag: Ito ang pisikal na 'certificate' ng lisensya mo. Ang Authority to Operate (3.7) ang karapatan, at ito ang papel na nagpapatunay.

⚠️ Dapat Tandaan: 3 taon ang validity at kailangan ng CBWC recommendation para sa renewal.
ai.prompt: Ipaliwanag nang simple ang Sec. 3.12 ng CAO 01-2022 tungkol sa Certificate of Authority to Operate. Magbigay ng practical customs example, ipaliwanag kung bakit ito umiiral, banggitin ang related provisions, at linawin ang common misconceptions.

paragraphs.text: Certificate of Identification (CI) — shall refer to the document certifying that the finished products to be exported is from a particular warehousing entry, and also to determine whether or not a particular entry is partially or fully consumed.

ai.title: Certificate of Identification (CI)
ai.content:
📖 Kahulugan: Dokumentong nagpapatunay na ang finished products na ie-export ay galing sa isang partikular na warehousing entry, at tumutulong malaman kung partially o fully consumed na ang entry.

💡 Simpleng Paliwanag: Ito ang 'link' ng finished product pabalik sa raw materials na in-import. Kailangan ito sa liquidation.

⚠️ Dapat Tandaan: Ayon sa 8.7, ang Customs Officer (Examiner) mula sa WAD ang nag-iisyu nito bago ang stuffing.
ai.prompt: Ipaliwanag nang simple ang Sec. 3.13 ng CAO 01-2022 tungkol sa Certificate of Identification (CI). Magbigay ng practical customs example, ipaliwanag kung bakit ito umiiral, banggitin ang related provisions, at linawin ang common misconceptions.

paragraphs.text: Certificate of Importer Accreditation — shall refer to the document issued by the Bureau to an entity registered as importer and recognized to electronically lodge goods declaration in the Bureau's existing registration system.

ai.title: Certificate of Importer Accreditation
ai.content:
📖 Kahulugan: Dokumentong inisyu ng Bureau sa entity na rehistrado bilang importer at kinikilalang puwedeng mag-lodge ng goods declaration electronically sa registration system ng Bureau.

💡 Simpleng Paliwanag: Hindi ka puwedeng mag-import kung hindi ka accredited. Ito ang 'ID' mo bilang importer.

⚠️ Dapat Tandaan: Kasama ito sa documentary requirements ng application (5.1.2.a) at renewal (5.4.1.a).
